subject: Post-call: capacity playbook + levers for sub-second streaming
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira@pioneerretail.com>, Jared Lewis <j.lewis@pioneerretail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: capacity playbook + levers for sub-second streaming

Hi Samira / Jared —

Great conversation this morning. Thanks for walking through the live demo and the 2-minute overview of your streaming use case. I promised a short recap and the pragmatic levers we think will get you to sub-second tail latency while keeping cost predictable. High-level notes below, followed by proposed next steps.

Quick recap of requirements you confirmed:
- Peak concurrent streams: ~3k concurrent users during promotions (burst to 5k)
- Typical request payload: 180–300 tokens with 1–3 streaming updates per session
- Target 95th pct latency: <= 800ms (goal: 500–600ms)
- Availability: multi-region failover; primary focus: US-east

Cost/perf levers we discussed (what we'll model):
1) Continuous batching: group short requests at router level with a 5–15ms batching window for higher GPU utilization without hurting median latency
2) KV/prefix caching: cache prompt prefixes and recent KV cache for repeat flows (useful for product-detail dialogs)
3) Quantization profiles: mixed pathway — FP16 for headroom, 8-bit variants for lower-cost long-running paths
4) Model variants & routing: low-cost 7B for background ranking, 30B/70B family for critical streaming paths; dynamic fallback on overload

Attachments: I attached a draft capacity playbook and a sample workload file so you can see the assumptions we'll run.

Proposed next steps:
- Redwood: run an initial cost/latency sensitivity matrix using your sample workload (I attached) — ETA: 48 hours (Ben + Karthik)
- Pioneer: confirm a representative traffic slice (1 hour of peak traffic) and a list of critical prompts we should prioritize for caching
- Schedule: 30-min follow-up next week to review numbers and agree on a pilot configuration

If this looks good I'll kick off the sensitivity runs and share results as an annotated spreadsheet.

Thanks —
Grace O'Connor
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_capacity_playbook_v1.pdf (PDF, 1.2MB)]
[Attachment: pioneer_sample_workload.json (JSON, 45KB)]

From: Samira Khan <samira@pioneerretail.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com>, Jared Lewis <j.lewis@pioneerretail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: capacity playbook + levers for sub-second streaming

Thanks Grace — this is exactly what we need. A few clarifying Qs before you run the sensitivity matrix: 

1) For continuous batching, can you include a scenario with both 5ms and 15ms windows and show the impact on 95th pct latency and cost per 1M tokens? Our concern is user experience during live promotions.
2) For caching, we'll send 12 example prompts — please show a scenario with 0%, 30%, and 60% prefix cache hit rates.
3) For quantization, we need guidance on fidelity trade-offs for reranking vs. generation. Reranking tolerates more aggressive quantization; generation less so.

Also, can you include a best-guess for the infra footprint (GPUs and nodes) for a pilot at 3k concurrent? We want a rough procurement timeline.

Thanks — Samira
Head of Product Engineering, Pioneer Retail

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Samira Khan <samira@pioneerretail.com>, Jared Lewis <j.lewis@pioneerretail.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 12:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: capacity playbook + levers for sub-second streaming

On it — starting with a back-of-envelope so Samira has something today. High-level assumptions:
- Workload: 250 tokens avg, streaming chunk ~40 tokens per update
- Concurrency target: 3k steady, 5k burst

Quick numbers (ballpark):
- No batching, FP16 large model: ~120 p95 requests/sec per a80-equivalent GPU -> would need ~25 GPUs for steady 3k concurrency (not optimized)
- 5ms continuous batching + prefix caching (30%): cuts effective token work by ~30% and increases GPU throughput to ~180 p95 reqs/sec -> ~17 GPUs
- 15ms batching + 60% cache + 8-bit quantization on background model variants -> ~260 p95 reqs/sec -> ~12 GPUs (but check quality delta on generation paths)

I'll run the sensitivity matrix for the specific scenarios Samira requested and produce a simple 'GPUs vs cost vs p95 latency' sheet. Karthik — can you confirm the expected latency hit for 8-bit on reranking vs streamed generation? If we can quantify that as +X ms or Y% quality delta we should be able to recommend safe switch points.

Ben
Solutions Engineering
[Attachment: quick_boe_numbers.csv (CSV, 12KB)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Samira Khan <samira@pioneerretail.com>, Jared Lewis <j.lewis@pioneerretail.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 17:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: capacity playbook + levers for sub-second streaming

Thanks — quick technical notes I will include in the run: 

- 8-bit quantization (int8) typically reduces model memory footprint ~2x and improves throughput ~1.5–1.8x versus FP16 for the same kernel, but expect tail latency variance to increase slightly. For reranking-only paths it's low risk; for streamed token-by-token generation we should only route lower-criticality sessions to int8 unless you run evaluation sets.
- Continuous batching: we should use adaptive windows (5ms base, up to 20ms during cold starts) and prioritize low-latency sessions with expedited routing. Batching parameters to sweep: window {5, 10, 15}ms; max batch size {64, 128}.
- KV cache: fingerprint recent prefixes at the router and maintain a hot-set in GPU memory for immediate reuse — model pathing needs to preserve KV slot compatibility across quantization variants.

I'll attach a CSV of quant profiles and a short runbook for the pilot. I recommend a pilot config: 12 GPUs (a80-equivalent) with 15ms batching, 30% cache target, FP16 on critical streams and int8 on rerank/gating. That should get you into the 500–700ms p95 band for the sample workload; we will refine with your actual 1-hour peak slice.

-Karthik
Applied ML / Inference Optimization
[Attachment: quant_profiles.csv (CSV, 6KB)]

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira@pioneerretail.com>, Jared Lewis <j.lewis@pioneerretail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Aug 2026 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: capacity playbook + levers for sub-second streaming

Samira — thanks for the quick turn. Per our plan we ran the sensitivity matrix against your sample workload and attached the annotated playbook. Highlights:
- Baseline (no batching, FP16): estimated 95th pct = ~1.2s, ~25 GPUs
- 5ms batching + 30% caching: p95 -> ~750–820ms, ~16–18 GPUs
- 15ms batching + 60% caching + int8 routing for reranks: p95 -> ~520–640ms, ~10–13 GPUs (quality trade-offs documented in the sheet)

Requested next steps:
1) Pioneer: send the 1-hour peak slice + the 12 critical prompts for caching (we still need the prompt list)
2) Redwood: schedule a 30-min cost-review on Mon 08/23 or Tue 08/24 — aim to lock a pilot configuration and pilot dates
3) Legal/procurement: if you want a dedicated capacity pilot, we'll loop in our sales and finance teams; otherwise hosted pilot is quickest.

I'll put the annotated spreadsheet and playbook in the Drive link and share a short recording of the numbers walkthrough.

Best —
Grace
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_capacity_playbook_v1.pdf (PDF, 1.2MB)]
